history.title: The rise of modern alpinism
history.text: European alpine climbing grew into a distinct pursuit during the 18th century. The first recorded ascent of Mont Blanc in 1786 is widely treated as a landmark in the history of modern alpinism.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing a snowy slope

history.title: From exploration to shared knowledge
history.text: Climbing history is also a record of local knowledge, changing equipment and teamwork. National park archives preserve expedition reports, route histories, rescues and lessons from earlier climbs.

image.alt: Climber looking toward a sunlit mountain ridge

styles.title: Alpine style
styles.text: A team carries its supplies and climbs continuously, rather than relying on a chain of stocked camps. The lighter approach can reduce time on a route, but it demands strong teamwork, sound judgement and self-sufficiency.

image.alt: Roped climber moving up a steep rock face

styles.title: Expedition style
styles.text: A longer expedition may use a base camp and staged higher camps to support acclimatization and carry loads. It requires more logistics and time; fixed ropes and supplemental oxygen are route choices, not guarantees of safety.

image.alt: Climber progressing on a large rock wall

techniques.title: Rope-team travel
techniques.text: Rope systems on glaciers or exposed ground only work when the whole team is trained in their use. Crevasse rescue, spacing and anchor decisions need hands-on practice with a qualified instructor.

image.alt: Climber using a rope system on a mountain

techniques.title: Rock movement and protection
techniques.text: Scrambling and rock climbing require route-finding, secure movement and protection appropriate to the terrain. Learn knots, belaying and anchor systems in a controlled setting before relying on them outdoors.

image.alt: Roped climber moving across a rock wall

techniques.title: Snow and ice travel
techniques.text: Crampons, an ice axe and avalanche equipment are useful only with the training to use them. Check the local avalanche bulletin and forecast, and change plans when conditions exceed your team's experience.

image.alt: Climber ascending a snow-covered ridge

shelter.title: Planned camps and mountain huts
shelter.text: Use designated camps, huts and established sites where available. Check access, booking, seasonal opening and local waste rules before departure; a shelter does not remove exposure or altitude risks.

image.alt: Mountaineer preparing equipment before a climb

shelter.title: Emergency bivouac
shelter.text: A bivouac is an unplanned night out, not a substitute for an itinerary. Carry weather-appropriate emergency insulation and shelter, tell someone your plan, and seek a safer descent or rescue when conditions allow.

image.alt: Mountaineer crossing a snowy slope in cold-weather gear

hazards.title: Altitude illness
hazards.text: Headache, nausea and unusual fatigue can be early signs of acute mountain sickness. Do not ascend with symptoms; worsening symptoms at rest, confusion or breathlessness require urgent descent and medical help.

image.alt: Climber ascending a high mountain slope

hazards.title: Weather, avalanche and falling debris
hazards.text: Wind, storms, unstable snow, rockfall and changing visibility can turn a familiar route into a serious hazard. Review current local forecasts and avalanche bulletins and agree on a turnaround plan.

image.alt: Climber roped on a steep snowy mountain face

hazards.title: Cold, exhaustion and delays
hazards.text: Cold injury, dehydration, fatigue and a slower-than-planned descent can compound other risks. Protect hands and feet, eat and drink regularly, monitor partners and keep enough reserve for the return.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing an icy waterfall

records.title: Highest above sea level
records.text: Mount Everest is Earth's highest mountain above sea level. Nepal and China announced a jointly measured height of 8,848.86 metres in 2020.

image.alt: Climber roped on a steep snowy slope

records.title: Highest outside Asia
records.text: Aconcagua, in Argentina's Andes, rises to 6,961 metres and is the highest mountain outside Asia.

image.alt: Mountaineer ascending a rugged rock face

records.title: Highest in North America
records.text: Denali's summit is 6,190 metres above sea level. The National Park Service publishes route histories, seasonal reports and climbing statistics for the Alaska Range.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing a high alpine slope

stories.title: Annapurna I · 1950
stories.text: Maurice Herzog and Louis Lachenal reached the summit of Annapurna I on 3 June 1950, the first confirmed ascent of an 8,000-metre peak. The descent and severe injuries became part of the expedition's history.

image.alt: Climber approaching a high mountain summit

stories.title: Everest · 1953
stories.text: Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary reached Everest's summit on 29 May 1953 as members of a much larger expedition. Their ascent is a team achievement, not a solo story.

image.alt: Mountaineer preparing for a high mountain climb

stories.title: Everest without bottled oxygen · 1978
stories.text: Reinhold Messner and Peter Habeler made the first ascent of Everest without supplemental oxygen in 1978, a landmark in high-altitude mountaineering. It does not make an oxygen-free ascent a safe or suitable goal for others.

image.alt: Solo mountaineer on a steep rock wall

organizations.title: UIAA
organizations.text: The International Climbing and Mountaineering Federation connects member associations worldwide and publishes equipment safety standards and climber guidance.

image.alt: Climber preparing rope and safety equipment

organizations.title: American Alpine Club
organizations.text: A United States climbing organization that supports climbers through education, publications, advocacy and member resources.

image.alt: Mountaineer crossing a snowy mountain slope

organizations.title: British Mountaineering Council
organizations.text: The BMC represents climbers, hill walkers and mountaineers in Britain and provides club, access and participation resources.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing a snow and rock slope

developments.title: Check certified gear and safety notices
developments.text: Safety labels and equipment notices can change. Check the exact model and current notices rather than relying on an old gear list.

image.alt: Climber on a steep alpine rock face

developments.title: Use live mountain information
developments.text: Check current season reports, mountain-specific forecasts and route conditions before planning a climb.

image.alt: Climber on a steep rock wall

guidelines.title: Plan for the whole team
guidelines.text: Choose a route that matches the least experienced team member, check permits and local rules, share an itinerary and emergency contact, and agree on turnaround times before leaving.

image.alt: Mountaineer climbing a steep mountain route

guidelines.title: Leave the mountain better
guidelines.text: Follow local waste and wildlife rules, stay on durable surfaces where advised, respect local communities and other climbers, and pack out what you bring in.

image.alt: Climber on a rock route in the mountains
